get.summary:
Gets the latest state of a long-running operation.  Clients can use this
method to poll the operation result at intervals as recommended by the API
service.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the operation resource.

post.summary:
Waits until the specified long-running operation is done or reaches at most
a specified timeout, returning the latest state.  If the operation is
already done, the latest state is immediately returned.  If the timeout
specified is greater than the default HTTP/RPC timeout, the HTTP/RPC
timeout is used.  If the server does not support this method, it returns
`google.rpc.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED`.
Note that this method is on a best-effort basis.  It may return the latest
state before the specified timeout (including immediately), meaning even an
immediate response is no guarantee that the operation is done.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the operation resource to wait on.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description:
The maximum duration to wait before timing out. If left blank, the wait
will be at most the time permitted by the underlying HTTP/RPC protocol.
If RPC context deadline is also specified, the shorter one will be used.

post.summary:
TriggerTenantWorkflow triggers a tenant-level workflow (e.g., inventory) for the
caller's tenant, fanning out to all eligible providers. Internally invokes the
same composer that runs during scheduled triggers, scoped to the caller's tenant
(the schedule policy is forced to is_global=false for the synthetic schedule).
post.description:
The tenant is derived from the request context (acontext.IdentityContext.GetTenant).
Permissions follow the same RBAC pattern as the other RPCs on this service.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
TriggerTenantWorkflowRequest triggers a tenant-level workflow for the caller's
tenant by composing tasks via the registered or generic composer.

Behavior mirrors the global-schedule path in knot: a synthetic schedule is built
for the caller's tenant with is_global=false, then handed to the appropriate
composer (e.g., InventoryTenantComposer for INVENTORY workflows). The resulting
task definitions are persisted as a single tenant-level workflow with provider
child workflow tasks.

At least one of {workflow_definition_id, workflow_type} must be supplied:
  * workflow_definition_id alone   - load that exact definition; its Type drives
                                     the composer choice.
  * workflow_type alone            - server resolves the canonical
                                     WorkflowDefinition for the type. For types
                                     backed by a hard-coded composer (currently
                                     INVENTORY) the server falls back to default
                                     values when no row exists. For types that
                                     depend on the generic composer (ANALYTICS,
                                     SUGGESTED_OWNERS, QUERY_CACHE_TIME_DEPENDENT)
                                     a row MUST exist because the recipe lives
                                     in WorkflowDefinition.task_definitions.
  * both                           - workflow_definition_id wins; workflow_type
                                     is validated to match WD.Type.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
- INVENTORY_PARENT_WF: Parent workflow type that creates child INVENTORY workflows via ANDROMEDA_WORKFLOW tasks
This type bypasses per-provider blocking for INVENTORY workflows, preventing deadlocks
 - SUGGESTED_OWNERS: Workflow type for resolving suggested owners from TSDB logs
 - DELTASYNC_SYNC: Workflow type for delta sync sync phase (reads DELTA mode resources from IR, publishes to Kepler)
Mutually exclusive with INVENTORY workflows per provider
 - ANALYTICS: Workflow type for analytics runs (behavior models, and future analytics tasks like lsp-eps, Galileo).
Scheduled via knot; runs at GLOBAL level. Managed by AnalyticsController.
 - ON_DEMAND_ANALYSIS: Generic on-demand analysis workflow. Routes to any service implementing ExecutionService.
Use for per-tenant, API-triggered analyses (ariel group anomaly, unused groups, etc.).
Independent concurrency from ANALYTICS — does not block behavior model runs.
 - TEST_CONNECTIVITY: Workflow type for testing provider connectivity
 - GRAPH_SYNC: Workflow type for async graph sync operations in polaris (ToolApplication, AccessPolicy, PolicyBinding).
 - GRAPH_JANITOR: Workflow type for the monthly graph soft-delete janitor. Scheduled via knot;
runs at GLOBAL level as a single Kubernetes Job (GRAPH_JANITOR task, KUBERNETES runtime).

parameters.name: clientRegistrationMode
parameters.description:
Who creates this connection's OAuth client. DYNAMIC registers Andromeda as a
client on the upstream authorization server via RFC 7591; MANUAL (the default,
and how onboarding works today) takes the client id, secret and endpoints from
connection.auth_profile as supplied and registers nothing upstream.

Under DYNAMIC the server re-runs the discovery chain itself rather than trusting
endpoints that came through the browser, since client-supplied metadata must not
steer an outbound registration, and fails the create when the authorization
server advertises no registration_endpoint.

Request-scoped on purpose: this is onboarding intent, and the durable record
of what happened is whether an McpDynamicClientRegistration row exists for the
resulting connection. See specs/agents/COOPER_OUTBOUND_DCR.md.

Note this RPC binds body to connection, not to *, so over REST this arrives as
a QUERY PARAMETER rather than in the request body. That is intentional and
matches CreateJitPolicyRequest.id and UpdateFavorites.id; do not switch the
binding to body star to move it, since that would change the existing request
shape for every caller.
Example: client_registration_mode DYNAMIC

 - CLIENT_REGISTRATION_MODE_UNSPECIFIED: Not specified by the caller. Read as MANUAL: never self-register a client
against a connection that did not explicitly ask for it.
 - DYNAMIC: Register Andromeda as a client on the upstream authorization server via RFC
7591. Fails the create if that server advertises no registration_endpoint,
rather than silently leaving a connection with no usable client.
Example: client_registration_mode DYNAMIC
 - MANUAL: The operator supplies the client id, secret and endpoints themselves, exactly
as onboarding works today. Andromeda registers nothing upstream.
Example: client_registration_mode MANUAL

post.summary:
DiscoverToolApplicationAuth runs the unauthenticated auth-discovery chain
against the application's MCP server URL - an initialize with no bearer, then
RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, then RFC 8414 authorization-server
metadata - and reports what it found.
post.description:
READ-ONLY and safe to retry: it registers no client and persists no
credentials. That is a hard constraint, not a convenience - RFC 7591 has no
get-or-create, so an endpoint that registered would mint a duplicate client on
the upstream every time the operator refreshed the page. Registration happens
later, inside CreateToolApplicationConnection, which is also what keeps the
issued client_secret from ever transiting the browser.

Called before the connection exists so the onboarding UI knows which form to
render - credential fields or none - and the subsequent create carries complete
data instead of leaving a half-configured connection behind. Application-scoped
because the MCP server URL lives on the application (AppMcpServerConfig), not
on a connection. See specs/agents/COOPER_OUTBOUND_DCR.md.

 - RESOURCE_TYPE_PAGERDUTY_SERVICE: 3204 reserved — user role assignments use RESOURCE_TYPE_PAGERDUTY_ROLE on
ScopeUserPolicyBinding; no separate external resource type is required.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_GRAFANA_USER: Grafana resource types
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_GRAFANA_ROLE: END-PROVIDERGEN: ExternalResourceType
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_GOOGLE_AGENT_ENGINE_AGENT: Google Agent Platform runtime-specific resource types
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_GEMINI_ENTERPRISE_APP: Gemini Enterprise resources
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CURSOR_DESKTOP_AGENT: Cooper sponsor-registered desktop agents (not inventory-sourced) — used
only for RegisterAgent / DeleteRegisteredAgent graph wiring.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_SELF_HOSTED_AGENT: Cooper self-hosted agent (operator-run runtime) resource family.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_DATADOG_USER: Datadog resource types — block 3840-3849. Deliberately outside the
AgentBlueprint block 3820-3829.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CODEX_DESKTOP_AGENT: OpenAI Codex desktop agent resource types (on-host RTR codex_inventory).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_GITHUB_COPILOT_AGENT: GitHub Copilot IDE agents discovered on the endpoint fleet via the
CrowdStrike RTR inventory (VS Code / JetBrains). Endpoint desktop-agent
family, block 3630-3639 (after Codex 3626-3629); NOT the Claude Platform
block 3800-3819 nor the AgentBlueprint block 3820-3829.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLOUDFLARE_USER: Cloudflare resource types — block 3500-3520 reserved.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN: Account-owned API token (NHI / service principal).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLOUDFLARE_MEMBER_PG: Member permission group (assignable to humans).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN_PG: Token-plane PG registry, shared by account- and user-owned tokens.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CURSOR_ACCOUNT: Cursor org/team roster resource types (Admin API ingest) with no
pre-existing desktop equivalent. Users / roles / agents reuse the
RESOURCE_TYPE_CURSOR_DESKTOP_* types above. 3613-3621 are reserved
(Cloudflare), so these start at 3622.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CURSOR_GROUP: Cursor billing/directory group (GET /teams/groups); optionally
SCIM-synced to an IdP directory group via directoryGroupId.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_RETOOL_USER: Retool resource types — block 3700-3719 reserved.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_RETOOL_OBJECT_ACCESS: Per-object access policy (use/edit/own/none access list) attached to a
Retool app/folder/resource/workflow scope. Distinct from
RESOURCE_TYPE_RETOOL_ROLE (org-level RBAC) so the two never collide in the
collector's per-proto mark-and-sweep.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_RETOOL_ACCESS_TOKEN: Retool API access token modeled as a non-human identity (NHI). The token
label is used as the NHI display name; its scopes become the permissions of
a per-token RESOURCE_TYPE_RETOOL_NHI_ROLE policy.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_RETOOL_NHI_ROLE: Per-NHI custom role synthesized from a Retool access token. One policy per
access token whose document carries the token scopes; the NHI is bound to
it directly via a provider-scope ScopeUserPolicyBinding. Distinct from
RESOURCE_TYPE_RETOOL_ROLE (org RBAC) and RESOURCE_TYPE_RETOOL_OBJECT_ACCESS
so the collector's per-proto mark-and-sweep never collides.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_USER: Claude Platform resource types — block 3800-3819 reserved.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_AGENT_INSTANCE: Runtime identity of a Claude Platform agent (the AgentInstance node),
distinct from the agent resource itself (RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_AGENT).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_API_KEY: Workspace API key from the Admin API (GET /v1/organizations/api_keys).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: WIF service account (svac_...) from the Admin API.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_ORG_ROLE: Organization-level member roles (admin, developer, billing, user, ...).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_WORKSPACE_ROLE: Workspace-scoped member roles (workspace_admin, workspace_user, ...).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_CONNECTION: Managed-agent MCP / built-in tool connection surface.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_TOOL_CLIENT: TOOL_CLIENT policy scoped to a Claude Platform agent connection.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_ENVIRONMENT: Managed Agents environment (org-scoped deployment target).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_KNOWLEDGE_BASE: Skill / knowledge source attached to a managed agent version.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_FEDERATION: Workload identity federation (org-scoped; Admin API federation_rules).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_VAULT: Managed Agents credential vault.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_CLAUDE_PLATFORM_AGENT_DELEGATION: Multi-agent delegation roster entry (coordinator instance → child instance).
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_AGENT_BLUEPRINT: AgentBlueprint resource types — block 3820-3829 reserved. Not
platform-specific: one shared pair reused across every blueprint platform
(Foundry, Copilot Studio, Gemini Enterprise, Bedrock AgentCore, Claude
Platform) — see records/proto/.../agent_blueprint.proto and
AgentTypeMessage.AGENT_BLUEPRINT.
 - RESOURCE_TYPE_AGENT_BLUEPRINT_INSTANCE: Runtime identity of the blueprint (the AgentInstance node, id = oauth_client_id),
distinct from the blueprint resource itself (RESOURCE_TYPE_AGENT_BLUEPRINT).

post.summary:
ConvertUsersToHuman creates one permanent override rule per affected
provider in that provider's UserDataMappingProfile, forcing the target users
to HUMAN identity type. Input users may span multiple providers; users
belonging to the same provider share a single rule.
To revert a conversion, delete the corresponding rule via the
UserDataMappingProfile rule management API.

ConvertUsersToService creates one permanent override rule per affected
provider in that provider's UserDataMappingProfile, forcing the target users
to SERVICE (NHI) identity type. The per-provider canonical NHI type is
derived server-side. Input users may span multiple providers; users
belonging to the same provider share a single rule.
To revert a conversion, delete the corresponding rule via the
UserDataMappingProfile rule management API.

Actions that can be done on Access reviews.

provider now that its cool-off period has elapsed. Example: NHI_KEY_DECOMMISSION.
 - NHI_KEY_KEEP: NHI key rotation, ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION mode only: leave the old key in place.
Terminal - the key is never prompted for again. Example: NHI_KEY_KEEP.

 - COUNTED_TOWARD_RECOMMENDATION: A passing included check counts toward an APPROVE recommendation.

- IN_PROGRESS: Check is in progress
 - PASS: All the conditions for the check passed
 - FAILED: Check failed
 - SKIPPED: not applicable
 - NO_DECISION: Not enough data to make a decision due to not enough data or model could not make a decision

AccessReviewReviewerStatusMessageAccessR.description:
- READY: Once the Campaign is ready with the snapshots and is waiting
activation the reviewer status is set to READY.
 - ASSIGNED: When the Campaign is activated and the reviewer has not made any
decision on the review and saved it.
 - COMPLETED: Reviewer has made a decision on the review as either
approved or denied.
 - SIGNED_OFF: reviewer has made the decision and signed off the review
This is automatically done by the system when the reviewer
signs off the campaign when all the reviews for that campaign are
completed.
 - NOT_REVIEWED: The campaign was force ended while this reviewer set was still outstanding, so it
never got signed off. Set by the UAR owner or admin.

AccessReviewRevocationStatusMessageAcces.description:
- UNSPECIFIED: The statuses can only go from ASSIGNED to any other state mentioned.
 - IN_PROGRESS: Andromeda is in the process of revoking the access will be retried infinitely
 - PENDING: Access needs to be revoked manually by the user
 - SKIPPED: UAR Owner has manually skipped revocation check
 - EXTERNALLY_REVOKED: User has marked the binding as revoked
 - FAILED: Failed to revoke access (used in the remediation campaign and the nhi key rotation campaign)
 - MARKED_FOR_DECOMMISSIONING: NHI key rotation, NOTIFICATION_AND_KEY_CREATION mode only: a replacement key was
created and the old key was marked for decommissioning. Terminal for that mode -
nothing further acts on the key. ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION mode deliberately uses
COOL_OFF_PERIOD_ACTIVE instead, so that a mode 2 row can never be claimed by the
decommission gate sweeper.
 - COOL_OFF_PERIOD_ACTIVE: NHI key rotation, ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION mode: a replacement key was created and the
old key was marked for decommissioning; the cool-off period is now running. The gate
sweeper owns rows in this state and nobody is on the hook for a decision yet. Once the clock
runs out the sweeper moves the row on to either PENDING_DECOMMISSION_DECISION or
OLD_KEY_STILL_IN_USE, so this value means strictly waiting on time.
Example: COOL_OFF_PERIOD_ACTIVE.
 - PENDING_DECOMMISSION_DECISION: NHI key rotation, ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION mode: the cool-off period elapsed and the old
key went quiet, so a reviewer now owes a decommission-or-keep decision.
Example: PENDING_DECOMMISSION_DECISION.
 - OLD_KEY_STILL_IN_USE: NHI key rotation, ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION mode: the cool-off period has elapsed, but the old
key is still being used, so no decision is asked for - deleting it would break whatever is
still calling it. The workload has not cut over to the replacement key. Distinct from
COOL_OFF_PERIOD_ACTIVE because the wait is no longer on the clock, it is on the customer, and
the two need different follow-up. Reverts to a decision once the key goes quiet.
Example: OLD_KEY_STILL_IN_USE.
 - DECOMMISSIONED: NHI key rotation, ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION mode: the old key was hard-deleted at the
provider. Terminal. Example: DECOMMISSIONED.

AccessReviewStatusMessageAccessReviewSta.description:
- ASSIGNED: The statuses can only go from ASSIGNED to any other state mentioned.
 - SKIPPED: The access will not be reviewed in the current campaign.
 - DENIED: Access is to be revoked, either automatically or manually.
 - DRAFT: intermidiate state before campaign state is set to review in progress
 - CHANGE_OWNER: Owner is being changed to a different identity (used with CHANGE_ASSET_OWNER action).
 - APPROVED_EXPLORER: EXCEPTION = 6;
 - NHI_KEY_DECOMMISSION: NHI key rotation, ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION mode only: the reviewer asked for the old
key to be deleted at the provider. Example: NHI_KEY_DECOMMISSION.
 - NHI_KEY_KEEP: NHI key rotation, ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION mode only: the reviewer chose to keep the
old key. Terminal. Example: NHI_KEY_KEEP.
 - NOT_REVIEWED: The campaign was force ended before this review got a decision, so no reviewer
ever made one. Set by the UAR owner or admin, never by a reviewer.

 - CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK: Anthropic Claude Agent SDK.

 - STRANDS: AWS Strands Agents SDK.

UAR_CAMPAIGN_NHI_KEY_ROTATION_DIGEST, which covers all of an owner's keys in one email. Kept so
the template row it refers to stays valid; no code sends this type anymore.

 - UAR_CAMPAIGN_NHI_KEY_DECOMMISSION_DECISION: ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION campaigns: one email per NHI owner listing old keys whose cool-off period
has elapsed and which now need a decommission-or-keep decision.
 - UAR_CAMPAIGN_REVOCATION_VALIDATION_STARTED: Every reviewer has signed off and the campaign moved to REVOCATION_VALIDATION_IN_PROGRESS.
Only campaigns with access_revocation_check_enabled reach that status, so the ones with no

CampaignActionTypeMessageCampaignActionT.description:
Actions that can be done on Campaign instances.

 - START_CAMPAIGN: Start preparing the snapshot.
 - REFRESH_CAMPAIGN: Begin a scheduled in-place refresh for explorer remediation campaigns.
 - ACTIVATE_CAMPAIGN: Start the campaign officially, and assigns reviewers the access reviews.
 - COMPLETE_CAMPAIGN: This acknowledges that the campaign is complete and all reviews have been given, either fully or partially.
 - CANCEL_CAMPAIGN: Cancel midway.
 - FORCE_END_CAMPAIGN: End a campaign that still has outstanding reviews. Valid only while the campaign is in
REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS, and only for a UAR_CAMPAIGN with no revocation check configured -
it jumps straight to report generation, which skips the revocation pipeline and would
cut the remediation and NHI key rotation lifecycles off mid-flight. Every review under
a reviewer who has not signed off is recorded as NOT_REVIEWED, the acting owner or admin
recorded as its actor, and the campaign ends in FORCE_ENDED rather than COMPLETED.

CampaignReviewerPersonaTypeMessageCampai.title: - ASSET_OWNER: For ASSET_OWNERSHIP campaigns - assigns the asset owner as reviewer

CampaignStatusTypeMessageCampaignStatus.description:
- DRAFT: Draft status is when the campaign is created but not yet ready to be started.
 - PREPARING: Campaign snapshot is being Prepared. This is triggered at a give or scheduled startTime.
The Andromeda system starts generating a snapshot of the data in the scope for the Campaign.
 - READY: Once the snapshot is ready, the campaign is ready to be reviewed by various personas.
 - REFRESH_IN_PROGRESS: Explorer remediation campaigns wait for pending revoke/JIT actions before re-snapshotting.
 - REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS: Review in progress is a waiting state. We accumulate all approvals within a given time frame.
This is a waiting state, and it is waiting for the reviewers to complete their reviews.
 - REVIEW_COMPLETED: Once all reviews are completed, the campaign is ready to be audited by the owners.
This is a waiting state, and it is waiting for the audit to be started.
 - CANCELLATION_IN_PROGRESS: Temporal state.
 - CANCELLED: A campaign can be cancelled at any time by the owners.
This is a terminal state.
 - COMPLETED: Audit completed is marked when the auditors mark it completed.
 - ARCHIVED: Archived is a terminal state.
 - FORCE_ENDED: The campaign was ended with outstanding reviews by the UAR owner or admin. Terminal,
and reached instead of COMPLETED so the audit trail keeps the two apart.

FeatureTypeMessageFeatureType.description:
- OKTA_DEFAULT_NHI: deprecated, do not use
 - ENTRA_DEFAULT_NHI: deprecated, do not use
 - SCOPED_ELIGIBILITY_DETAILS: If enabled, flattens out eligibility details at a per scope level.
Moves away from eligibleResourceGroups nested structure under eligibilityDetails.
 - OUT_OF_BAND_ELIGIBILITY_SYNC: When enabled, eligibilities can be synced to graphdb out of band via debezium notifications (legacy).
 - ADHOC_ANALYTICS_DASHBOARD: New experimendal adhoc analytics dashboard features
 - OBO_DISCOVERY: Feature flag to enable OAuth token/OBO (On Behalf Of) discovery for Google Workspace and Entra
 - WORKFLOW_INTROSPECTION: Feature flag to enable workflow introspection logging on completion
When enabled, logs inventory statistics summary and raises alerts for failures
 - AGENTS: Feature flag to enable agents dashboard in UI
 - INVENTORY_IRM_BATCH_WRITE: Feature flag to enable batched inventory resource mapping writes.
Rollout can be scoped per handler/path incrementally.
 - RECOMMENDATION_ENGINE_INVENTORY_TRIGGER: Controls whether the inventory workflow chain triggers the recommendation-engine
per-tenant pipeline after query cache completes.
Enabled by default. Disable per tenant to stop rec-engine from being triggered
from inventory without redeploying.
 - ACCOUNT_RECOMENDATIONS_CONFIGURED: Controls whether account-level recommendation tasks are computed for a tenant.
Enabled by default. Disable per tenant to skip account-level fetches
 - USER_ATTRIBUTES: Feature flag to enable user attribute ingestion and storage in PostgreSQL.
When enabled, IDP and HR attributes are persisted per-user and exposed via GraphQL.
 - WEBHOOK_CREATION: Controls whether the webhook creation UI is enabled.
 - CHANNELBOT_V2: When enabled, beacon sends the enriched AccessRequestNotificationPayload
(v2) to the channelbot service instead of the minimal v1 payload.
 - DELTA_APIS_INVENTORY: Controls delta inventory sync (delta API-based incremental sync for
providers that support it, e.g. Entra group memberships).
 - ENTRA_MAILBOX_NHI_DETECTION: Controls mailbox NHI detection in Entra. When enabled, per-user
mailboxSettings API calls identify shared/room/equipment mailboxes as NHIs.
 - STREAMING_INVENTORY_DUMP: STREAMING_INVENTORY_DUMP enables the streaming write architecture for S3 inventory dump.
When active, records flow directly to gzip files as they arrive (no in-memory hierarchy).
Only activate after production metrics show memory pressure or lock contention.
Falls back to improved in-memory S3 dump when not activated.
 - ANDROMEDATESTAPP: This should not be flipped to enabled ever. only for development testing in ci for
andromeda test app.
 - PAGERDUTY: BEGIN-PROVIDERGEN: FeatureType
(auto-generated by tools/providergen from providers/<name>/provider.yaml; do not edit by hand.)
 - WEBEX: END-PROVIDERGEN: FeatureType
 - SELF_HOSTED_AGENT: Gates the Custom / Self-Hosted agent platform, paired with
PROVIDER_TYPE_SELF_HOSTED_AGENT. The name must match that provider type's
feature_type exactly: the pairing is resolved by string, so a mismatch
makes every read of the provider log "invalid feature type".
 - EXTERNAL_RISK_SIGNAL: Gates the EXTERNAL_RISK_SIGNAL JIT auto-approval check, which denies
auto-approval while the requester has an unresolved endpoint detection.
EARLY_ACCESS so it resolves to ENABLED in dev/test and shadow-deploys
elsewhere until a tenant opts in.
 - UNRESTRICTED_APP_UPC_CLEANUP: When enabled, removes stale USER_PROVIDER_CONNECTION edges (and dependent IPB/cache
edges) on unrestricted IDP application providers. Unrestricted apps intentionally
skip UPC computation; this cleans legacy UPC from when the app was restricted or
after isAppRoleAssignmentRequired transitions true -> false.
 - ENTRA_PIM_ELIGIBILITY_INGESTION: When enabled, the Entra ingester collects PIM (Privileged Identity Management)
eligible assignments (directory role + group membership eligibilities) and Kepler
upserts them as managed PolicyEligibilityMappings. Off by default; this side-effects
eligibility config, so enable per tenant after validation.
 - AZURE_PIM_ELIGIBILITY_INGESTION: When enabled, the Azure ingester collects Azure resource PIM (ARM role eligibility
schedule instances) at subscription and resource-group scope and Kepler upserts them as
managed PolicyEligibilityMappings (account-scoped, with a resource-group constraint for
RG-scoped eligibilities). Management-group and below-resource-group scopes are skipped.
Off by default; this side-effects eligibility config, so enable per tenant after validation.
 - INVENTORY_DIGEST_BATCHING: Feature flag to enable batched/deduplicated inventory digest task processing
in kepler (policy, app binding, group membership handlers).
 - GROUP_ATTRIBUTES: Feature flag to enable IDP group attribute ingestion and storage in PostgreSQL.
When enabled, IDP group attributes are persisted per-group and exposed via GraphQL.
 - FALLBACK_AUDIT_EVENTS: Gates the EventInterceptor fallback that emits CONFIG_* audit
events for non-GET andromeda.api methods lacking an explicit event
mapping/annotation. Kept in DEVELOPMENT so it can be rolled out per
tenant and rolled back without a deploy.
 - INCREMENTAL_INVENTORY_QUERY_CACHE: When enabled, the inventory-dependent query cache runs incrementally:
each post-sync run recomputes only entities whose graph updatedAt is newer
than the last successful run watermark, instead of a full tenant scan.
DEVELOPMENT status auto-enables on DEV/TEST environments only.
 - INVENTORY_STORE_V2: Per-tenant opt-in for the vertically-split, partition-by-tenant inventory store
(inventory_scopes + inventory_resource_states + inventory_resource_data).
DEACTIVATED so it stays off globally and is enabled one tenant at a time via the
tenant internal config override; see driver_postgres.go and IsInventoryStoreV2FeatureEnabled.
 - INVENTORY_COLLECT_O_CHANGES: Per-tenant opt-in for O(changes) inventory collect on the INVENTORY_STORE_V2 driver store.
When enabled, a collect sweep skips writing driver rows for unchanged resources and instead
records seen keys in a lightweight presence set; MarkStaleResources detects deletions via a
presence anti-join instead of bumping resource_sync_time on every unchanged row. Requires
INVENTORY_STORE_V2. DEACTIVATED so it stays off globally and is enabled one tenant at a time.
See driver_postgres.go presence-set path.
 - REST_INCLUDE_NAME: REST responses rewrite reference-UUID fields to uuid#name when the
request carries include_name=true (AS-12729). Example: providerId
becomes 31f4ee04-...#my-provider-1.
 - AGENT_ONBOARDING: Gates the agent onboarding operation that migrates
discovered agents to the Andromeda gateway
 - APPLICATION_KEY_INSIGHTS: Gates ingestion of native application-provider key material (Teleport
bot join tokens, Retool access tokens). These plugins call provider APIs
that need extra scopes, so the feature stays disabled in production until
permissions are confirmed per tenant; DEVELOPMENT auto-enables it in dev
and test environments.
 - NHI_KEY_LIFECYCLE_MANAGEMENT: Gates the AWS-only NHI (non-human-identity) lifecycle management config
section: automated secret/key rotation via a vault integration (an
Integration whose category is VAULT).
 - CONNECTION_IDENTITY_CORRELATION: Gates the connection-to-NHI correlation surfaces: the `Identity` column
on the agent applications list, the NHI `Agents` tab, and the
corresponding access-graph extensions. See
specs/agents/COOPER_CONNECTION_NHI_CORRELATION.md.
 - TACHYON_REFRESH_APPLICATION_PROVIDERS: Includes this tenant's application providers (IDP_APPLICATION,
CUSTOM_APPLICATION, PINGONE) in TenantCacheRefreshTrigger, so their
configured assignments are rebuilt on inventory completion like any other
provider instead of waiting on the cache TTL. See AS-23596. Off by default:
a tenant can have many application registrations, and the trigger runs
hardRefresh sequentially while inventory completion blocks on it, so this
is intended for test tenants only, not for tenant-wide/prod use.
 - SKIP_UNCONFIGURED_PROVIDER_SYNC: Skips the inventory-sync/test-connectivity activity for a provider with no ProviderConfiguration attached yet, instead of failing the workflow
 - OKTA_DELTA_INVENTORY: Okta delta inventory: delta user/group lists plus the System Log change feed on incremental syncs; paired with DELTA_APIS_INVENTORY, mirroring how ENTRA_BATCHED_GM pairs with it.
 - CROWDSTRIKE_ENDPOINT_COLLECTOR: Runs the CrowdStrike endpoint collector: a background sweep, scheduled
independently of the inventory sync, that reaches endpoints the sync has
never managed to collect from and stores what they report in
mdm_inventory_snapshots. The inventory sync is unchanged and simply finds
more to replay for endpoints it cannot reach itself. Off by default because
it opens additional RTR sessions against the tenant Falcon instance, and
tenant-wide, so enabling it sweeps every CrowdStrike provider the tenant has.
 - CONVERSATIONAL_AI_STREAMING: Client-side switch for streaming the Cosmos AI answer. It gates only the UI:
with the flag off, every prompt takes the unary path, and the streaming
endpoints stay reachable but unused. It exists so a blocked customer can be
moved off streaming without a backend change or a release.

 - RISK_ACCEPTED: Identities whos risk has been accepted in the account. The standing policies
that have high blast risk are not included in account's risk calculation.
 - SUPER_ADMIN: Identities that have super admin privileges like IAM admin permissions like <TBD>

Local IAM users when provider is setup with the AWS IDC
 - NON_COMPLIANT: Identity state is non-compliant across the IDP (deactivated) and Provider (active).

Kept at 54/55/56 to stay aligned with ProviderIdentitySignificanceType, where 51/52 are taken

 - KEY_INACTIVE_30_90_DAYS: These would replace the inactive Key types

discrete KEY_INACTIVE buckets wired in Go.

If identity has one of the sources (incarnation) as a privileged user defined

 - PASSWORD_ROTATION_OVERDUE: Password rotation is overdue for the identity based on AD group membership tier.

JitPolicyTransactionStatusTypeMessageAcc.description:
- CREATED: Initial status of the JitPolicyRequest when it is created by the User.
The JitPolicyTransaction is created right after the JitPolicyRequest is created
with this status (as a transaction). The transaction, is initialized with
status "CREATED".
 - REQUEST_ANALYSIS_IN_PROGRESS: A JitPolicyTransaction is marked SUBMITTED once the JIT Controller reads/registers
the "CREATED" JIT Request.
The JIT Controller must be active to mark the JIT Transaction as SUBMITTED.
As part of the Controller processing, the Request is also sent for Request Analysis
by the Andromeda system.
 - REQUEST_ANALYZED: A JitPolicyTransaction is marked REQUEST_ANALYZED when the JIT Controller gets
a response from the analyzer system.
As part of the Controller processing, the Request is also assigned Reviewers
and Reviewers are notified. The Reviewers can, at this point, view the analyzed
JIT Policy Request, and approval/reject the Request.
 - REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS: JitPolicyRequest is marked REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS once initial set of Reviewers are notified.
Andromeda System then waits for the Approval/Rejection/Timeout of the Reviewers.
The Request stays in this state until all the required Reviewers have responded.
 - APPROVED: JitPolicyRequest is APPROVED once all Reviewers have APPROVED.
 - SCHEDULED_FOR_PROVISIONING: JitPolicyRequest is SCHEDULED_FOR_PROVISIONING for a future time, once it has been APPROVED.
The startTime for the Provisioning is asked as part of the JitPolicyRequest creation.
 - WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_PROVISIONING: The Request is WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_PROVISIONING to be completed, when request profile has
manual provisioning/deprovisioning enabled.
 - PROVISIONING_IN_PROGRESS: Transient
 - PROVISIONED: JIT Session is PROVISIONED and the User can access the resources.
After the Provisioning, the Request is scheduled for Deprovisioning.
 - DEPROVISIONING_IN_PROGRESS: Transient
 - WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_DEPROVISIONING: The Request is WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_DEPROVISIONING to be completed, when request profile has
manual provisioning/deprovisioning enabled.
 - DEPROVISIONED: JIT Session is DEPROVISIONED and the User can no longer access the resources.
After the successful DeProvisioning, the JIT Controller schedules a check to validate whether
the Policy has been Deprovisioned for the User.
 - SESSION_ANALYSIS_PENDING: Once the JIT Controller detects a deprovisioned action, the Session is marked
as pending for analysis by the Session summarizer.
 - CANCELLATION_IN_PROGRESS: Access request status is marked as CANCELLATION_IN_PROGRESS when:
1. The Requester manually ends the session. Here the controller will be cleaning up
  running processes for the request.
 - REJECTED: JitPolicyRequest is REJECTED once a Reviewer rejects the Request.
This is a terminal state.
 - DEPROVISIONING_FAILED: JIT Request is marked as DEPROVISIONING_FAILED when the deprovisioning fails.
Deprovisioning can be retried using the bulk retrigger deprovisioning API.
 - PROVISIONING_FAILED: JIT Request is marked as PROVISIONING_FAILED when the provisioning fails.
Provisioning can be retried using the bulk retrigger provisioning API.
 - FAILED: JIT processing failed during any of the previous steps.
This is a terminal state.
 - TIMED_OUT: Request is Time out when start time passes and review is not approved.
This is a terminal state.
 - CLOSED: Request is closed before PROVISIONED.
This is a terminal state.
 - SKIPPED: When the the access is already provisioned via some other route
we might want to skip provisioning / deprovisioning.
 - COMPLETED: JitPolicyRequest is marked as COMPLETED from either:
1. The Requester manually ending the Session after it is Provisioned, or
2. The Controller archiving it once the Session has been analyzed in the end, or
This is a terminal state.

KeySignificanceCategoryMessageKeySignifi.description:
- KEY_EXPIRATION: Bucketed days-until-expiry for active keys, plus a sentinel
bucket for providers/keys without an expiry (NO_EXPIRY).
 - LIFECYCLE: Andromeda key lifecycle (rotation / decommission / deactivate grace).

KeySignificanceTypeMessageKeySignificanc.description:
- UNUSED_30_90_DAYS: Category: ACTIVITY
 - OLD_KEY_ACTIVE: Old key (already MARKED_FOR_DECOMMISSIONING) is still being used within
NHIKeyRotationCadence.old_key_inactivity_period_days — customer hasn't cut
over to the successor yet. Orthogonal to LIFECYCLE — a key can be both
MARKED_FOR_DECOMMISSIONING and OLD_KEY_ACTIVE at once.
 - UNUSED_30_DAYS_PLUS: Cumulative unused buckets (N+ days) — the form keyOpsInsight reports, and
the per-key twin of the identity/user KEY_UNUSED_* family. Each is the OR of
the discrete interval buckets at or below its threshold; the graph stays
discrete (accessKeyInactive{3090,90180,180365,365DaysPlus}), so there is no
write-path change.

There is no fourth value to add: UNUSED_365_DAYS_PLUS above is already
open-ended and already UNUSED-named, so it serves as the deepest cumulative
bucket unchanged. Its derived twin was renamed KEY_UNUSED_365_DAYS_PLUS (same
number 4) so the whole cumulative set reads UNUSED on both enums. Same
reasoning as wireCumulativeInactivity, which likewise reuses the open-ended
INACTIVE_365_DAYS_PLUS rather than minting a duplicate.
 - ROTATION_DUE: Category: LIFECYCLE — see specs/nhi-key-lifecycle.md
Key is usable, outside Andromeda TTL, and not yet marked for decommissioning.
 - MARKED_FOR_DECOMMISSIONING: A successor key has been chosen for this key. Fires immediately on
decommission; no grace-period wait, no bearing on activity.
 - DECOMMISSIONING_REJECTED: An explicit action rejected/cancelled this key's pending decommission.
Written by the NHI_KEY_KEEP decision in ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION campaigns,
which sets UserAccessKey.decommissioning_rejected.

 - MSSQL_ASYMMETRIC_KEY: SQL Server ASYMMETRIC_KEY_MAPPED_LOGIN / ASYMMETRIC_KEY_MAPPED_USER -- login/user

 - DATADOG_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: Datadog personal access token (ddpat_). Owned by a user or service account
and carries its own scopes.

against a connection that did not explicitly ask for it.
 - DYNAMIC: Register Andromeda as a client on the upstream authorization server via RFC
7591. Fails the create if that server advertises no registration_endpoint,
rather than silently leaving a connection with no usable client.

NhiKeyRotationCampaignModeMessageNhiKeyR.description:
- NOTIFICATION_ONLY: Snapshot due-for-rotation keys and email a reminder per reviewer. No provider mutations.
 - NOTIFICATION_AND_KEY_CREATION: For each due key: create a replacement via relay, mark the old key for decommissioning
in the graph, then email the reviewer the old/new key pair. Replaces the plain reminder.
The old key is left in place indefinitely.
 - ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION: Everything NOTIFICATION_AND_KEY_CREATION does, and then: once the old key has been quiet
past NHIKeyRotationCadence.old_key_deletion_cooldown_days, ask its reviewer to either
decommission it (hard-delete at the provider) or keep it. Keep is terminal - the key is
never prompted for again. An undecided key stays pending indefinitely; nothing is deleted
without an explicit decision. Example: ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION.

is too broad.
 - NHI_SUBTYPE_CHANGED: Stays an NHI, but the NHI subtype changes.
 - ATTRIBUTION_ONLY: Same classification, but a different rule now gets the credit. No
user-visible impact; useful for spotting a rule shadowing another.
 - MATCHED_BUT_SKIPPED: The rule matched, but its action declined to act. Looks like impact and
is not.
 - BLOCKED_BY_OVERRIDE: An admin conversion rule protects this user, so the candidate never
ran against them.

PromptContextMessagePromptContextType.description:
- UNSPECIFIED: Default fallback. Used when the user's intent is ambiguous, conversational chatter,
or does not cleanly map to specific Andromeda modules.
 - ACCESS_MANAGEMENT: Handles queries related to permissions rightsizing, dynamic least privilege,
and Just-In-Time (JIT) access requests. Route here if the user asks to modify,
grant, revoke, request, or approve permissions, entitlements, or roles for
human users or non-human identities (like API keys, service accounts, or tokens).
 - IDENTITY_GOVERNANCE: Handles queries regarding Identity Lifecycle events like Join, Move, Leave
functions often called as JML.
Route here if the user asks about onboarding or offboarding identities
 - SECURITY_INSIGHTS_AND_SUGGESTIONS: Handles queries regarding real-time identity risk scoring, behavioral analysis,
anomaly detection, and operational threat hunting. Route here if the user asks
about identity breaches, suspicious activity logs, privilege escalations,
break-glass accounts missing MFA, or needs remediation suggestions for security gaps.
 - AGENTIC_AI: Handles queries regarding the security, lifecycle, permissions, and behavior
of autonomous AI agents, machine identities, and automated LLM workflow extensions
operating within the cloud or SaaS environment. Route here if the user explicitly
asks about monitoring or securing Agentic AI and machine-era infrastructure.
 - USER_ACCESS_REVIEWS: Handles queries regarding user access reviews (UAR),
compliance frameworks (e.g., PCI DSS, ISO 27001, NY DFS), and identity inventory.
Route here if the user asks about scheduling access reviews, auditing stale accounts,
tracking human/NHI identity sprawl, or pulling compliance posture evidence.

gracePeriodSeconds.description:
How long the PREVIOUS secret keeps working, giving the operator time to
redeploy. Unset means the server default. Explicit zero revokes the old
secret immediately — the correct choice when rotating because it leaked,
and the wrong one for routine rotation, since it breaks the agent until it
is redeployed.

Optional rather than a plain int64 so unset and an explicit 0 stay
distinguishable; those two mean opposite things here. A scalar seconds
field rather than google.protobuf.Duration because Duration is not
currently supported by the unmarshal codegen.
Example: "3600"

ServiceIdentitySignificanceTypeMessageSe.description:
- CROSS_ACCOUNT_WITH_CRITICALITY_ESCALATION: Anyone of the owners is a stale owner or deactived owner.
Cross account access with criticality escalation
 - SUPER_ADMIN: Deprecated
 - EKS_CLUSTER_NOT_FOUND: If a service identity has some inconsistency
 - MULTIPLE_NHIS_SHARE_SAME_AWS_ROLE: multiple service identities that were discovered from the same role
 - INACTIVE_30_90_DAYS: last activity seen.
 - INACTIVE_30_DAYS_PLUS: Cumulative inactivity buckets (N+ days). Filter-only; OR of discrete buckets wired in Go.
 - KEY_UNUSED_30_DAYS_PLUS: Cumulative key-unused buckets (N+ days). Filter-only; OR of the
discrete KEY_INACTIVE buckets wired in Go.
 - NHI_WITH_NO_POLICY_BINDINGS: NHI with no policy bindings
 - OVERPRIVILEGED_ROLE: NHI has over provisioned permissions for this assignment in the context.
 - UNUSED_ROLE: NHI has unused assignments permissions in the context.
 - EXTERNAL_CLIENT: If an NHI is externally used. This will automatically include AWS external NHIs and
any NHI that is local but used by an external client.
 - FEDERATED_IDENTITY: GCP workload identity pool synthetic principal or an NHI impersonated by that principal.
 - CREDENTIAL_WITH_PASSWORD: Credential insights — independently computed buckets describing how an NHI
can authenticate. An NHI may match multiple buckets simultaneously (e.g.
an IAM User with both console password access and an enabled access key
carries both PASSWORD and EXPLICIT_KEY). NO_USABLE_CREDENTIALS is the
negation of the other three: it fires iff the NHI has no password, no
usable explicit key, and no implicit credential mechanism.

Source of truth per bucket:
  PASSWORD     — bool `has_password_credential` set by the ingester on
                 the bound User node (provider-specific signal — e.g.
                 AWS IAM LoginProfile, Okta credentials.password).
  EXPLICIT_KEY — derived in querycache from UserAccessKey rows
                 (`isEnabled = true` AND not past `keyExpiresAt`).
  IMPLICIT_KEY — bool `has_implicit_key_credential` set by the ingester
                 on the bound User node based on the NHI subtype
                 (instance-profile, managed identity, etc.).
  NO_USABLE_CREDENTIALS — pure Cypher negation of the above three.
 - RECENT_FAILED_ACTIONS: Service identity has had at least one error/failed provider action
(error_lookup.is_error = true) within the recent lookback window (30 days).
 - USED_BY_AGENT: Service identity is the resolved credential behind at least one
Agent's onboarded application connection (ToolApplicationConnection.
resolved_identity_id), i.e. some Agent effectively authenticates as
this NHI -- see specs/agents/COOPER_CONNECTION_NHI_CORRELATION.md.
 - HAS_AGENTIC_ACTIVITY: Service identity (NHI) has at least one github_agentic_activity row
resolving to it - an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, an MCP
client, etc.) drove GitHub activity on its behalf. Computed from
ClickHouse, not gated by identity type.

ToolProvenanceEnumToolProvenance.description:
- BUILT_IN: Platform-published / first-party / "shared_*" — included in the
Power Platform global gallery; not in the tenant's `/connectors`
table. Examples: shared_sharepointonline, shared_microsoftdataverse_mcpserver.
 - CUSTOM: Tenant-imported (maker uploaded a Swagger / authored a custom
connector). Present in the tenant's Dataverse `/connectors` table.

ToolTypeEnumToolType.description:
- MCP_SERVER: MCP server — speaks Model Context Protocol over streamable-HTTP/SSE.
Detected via /mcpservers row, x-ms-agentic-protocol on the connector
Swagger, or `kind: ModelContextProtocolMetadata` in the action YAML.
 - DATA_CONNECTOR: REST connector — the conventional Power Platform connector shape
(Swagger-described HTTP). Covers BOTH first-party shared_* connectors
(SharePoint, Teams, Salesforce) and tenant-imported custom connectors;
the BUILT_IN vs CUSTOM split lives on ToolProvenanceEnum, not here.
Name is `DATA_CONNECTOR` for backward compat with the legacy graph
enum — semantically equivalent to "REST connector".
 - A2A_SERVER: Agent-to-Agent server — speaks the A2A protocol. Reserved for when
Microsoft/anyone ships A2A on Power Platform; classifier doesn't emit
this yet but the value is here so downstream filters don't need a
schema bump when it lands.

UserAttributeMessageUserAttributeMessage.description:
- MANAGER_NAME: Manager Attributes
 - LOCATION_ZIP_CODE: Location Attributes. using location as prefix as
state conflicts with the existing identity state attribute
 - FIRST_NAME: currently supported only for HRMS User
Will not be persisted into graph
will only be used to populate graph USER name field
 - PROFILE_NAME: below will NOT be persisted into graph
not supported for IDP user and HRMS user
 - CUSTOM_FIELD_1: Custom fields for flexible attribute mapping
 - EXTERNAL_ID: The provider-native external ID of the user (user.id as published by the ingester).
Used by admin-issued identity-type conversion rules. The API accepts Andromeda UUIDs
and resolves them to external IDs at rule-creation time so kepler can match without
an extra DB lookup during rule evaluation.

UserSignificanceTypeMessageUserSignifica.description:
- ACCOUNT_OWNER: Users that are marked owners for an account.
 - ADMIN_PRIVILEGES: User has admin level privileges in the account determined by either access to
managed roles like AWSAdministratorAccess or IAM admin permissions like <TBD>
 - SUPER_ADMIN: Users that have super admin privileges like IAM admin permissions like <TBD>
 - LOCAL_USER: IDC user with local IAM Users
Local IAM users when provider is setup with the AWS IDC
 - STALE: User is stale
 - HIGH_BLAST_RISK: User has high blast risk
 - DEACTIVATED_USER_WITH_POLICY_BINDINGS: Deactivated user with policy bindings
 - MERGE_RULE_CONFLICT: User experienced merge rule conflict during inline identity merge
 - PRIVILEGED_USER: User flagged as privileged by the privileged-user CEL rule (User.is_privileged_user = true).
 - INACTIVE_30_DAYS_PLUS: Cumulative inactivity buckets (N+ days). Filter-only; OR of discrete buckets wired in Go.
 - KEY_UNUSED_30_DAYS_PLUS: Cumulative key-unused buckets (N+ days). Filter-only; OR of the
discrete KEY_INACTIVE buckets wired in Go.
 - PASSWORD_ROTATION_OVERDUE: Password rotation is overdue for the user based on AD group membership tier.
 - KEY_EXPIRES_LESS_THAN_14_DAYS: User has at least one enabled access key expiring in under 14 days.
 - KEY_HAS_NO_EXPIRY: User has at least one access key with no expiry set.
 - NO_LOGS: User has no activity logs on any provider that ingests logs.
 - HAS_AGENTIC_ACTIVITY: User (the GitHub-specific account, human-owned or NHI/App/PAT-owned) has
at least one github_agentic_activity row resolving to it - an AI coding
agent drove GitHub activity through this account. Computed from
ClickHouse, not gated by identity type.

WorkflowLevelMessageWorkflowLevel.title:
- GLOBAL: Global workflows orchestrate across all tenants (no tenant_id, no provider_id)
 - TENANT: Tenant workflows orchestrate providers within a single tenant (has tenant_id, no provider_id)
 - PROVIDER: Provider workflows are specific to one provider (has tenant_id and provider_id)

WorkflowStateMessageWorkflowState.description:
- INCOMPLETE_CONFIGURATION: Synthetic value: the provider has no configuration attached yet. Never written to a
real workflow row - only ever returned directly by the provider inventory-status resolver.

WorkflowTypeMessageWorkflowType.description:
- INVENTORY_PARENT_WF: Parent workflow type that creates child INVENTORY workflows via ANDROMEDA_WORKFLOW tasks
This type bypasses per-provider blocking for INVENTORY workflows, preventing deadlocks
 - SUGGESTED_OWNERS: Workflow type for resolving suggested owners from TSDB logs
 - DELTASYNC_SYNC: Workflow type for delta sync sync phase (reads DELTA mode resources from IR, publishes to Kepler)
Mutually exclusive with INVENTORY workflows per provider
 - ANALYTICS: Workflow type for analytics runs (behavior models, and future analytics tasks like lsp-eps, Galileo).
Scheduled via knot; runs at GLOBAL level. Managed by AnalyticsController.
 - ON_DEMAND_ANALYSIS: Generic on-demand analysis workflow. Routes to any service implementing ExecutionService.
Use for per-tenant, API-triggered analyses (ariel group anomaly, unused groups, etc.).
Independent concurrency from ANALYTICS — does not block behavior model runs.
 - TEST_CONNECTIVITY: Workflow type for testing provider connectivity
 - GRAPH_SYNC: Workflow type for async graph sync operations in polaris (ToolApplication, AccessPolicy, PolicyBinding).
 - GRAPH_JANITOR: Workflow type for the monthly graph soft-delete janitor. Scheduled via knot;
runs at GLOBAL level as a single Kubernetes Job (GRAPH_JANITOR task, KUBERNETES runtime).

id.description: Unique identifier for this turn (one prompt + one outcome).

conversationId.description: Logical link to config DB aiagent_conversations.id. Unset for standalone turns.

sequence.description: Order within a conversation. Unset when conversation_id is unset.

prompt.description: User input text. Empty for future non-text types; see prompt_payload.

promptPayload.description: Inbound request as jsonb (fields not stored in columns above).

responsePayload.description: Structured agent output as jsonb (ExplorerAgentResponse, JIT/UAR data, etc.).

metadata.description:
Ops telemetry as jsonb. Conventional keys: prompt_tokens_count,
completion_tokens_count, model_id, latency_ms, rejection_stage,
domain_status, tool_calls.

aiagentConversationTurn.description:
ConversationTurn is one persisted user prompt and agent outcome (audit, history
rehydration, and training export).

Table: aiagent_conversation_turns (COMPANION database). Thread metadata lives
in config DB (aiagent_conversations); conversation_id is a logical reference
only — no cross-database FK.

Agent-specific request/response shapes live in prompt_payload / response_payload
(jsonb). Ops telemetry lives in metadata (jsonb).

Enum fields use andromeda.api.models.config enums (shared with aiagent.proto).

`created_at` / `deleted_at` are injected by codegen. When conversation_id is
unset, the turn is a standalone event keyed by tenant_id + identity_id.

applicationId.title:

Display name of the DISCOVERED application. Historically named name; it holds
the discovered app name, not the onboarded one. Prefer discovered_application_name
and onboarded_application_name below for new consumers.
Example: Github PAT

Display name of the discovered application (same value as name; added for clarity).
Example: Github PAT

Display name of the matched ONBOARDED application (what the agent binds to).

source.description: How this match was determined (heuristic vs self vs user override).

agentId.title:
Logical Agent id this readiness describes.
Example: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890

tenantId.title:
Tenant that owns the agent.
Example: 9c719c8f-bf6c-40cd-80bd-e18f671411f3

appsToOnboard.description:
Discovered apps with no equivalent onboarded app; these must be onboarded
before the agent can become ELIGIBLE.

Discovered apps matched to an equivalent onboarded app; the agent will be
bound to the onboarded app when EnsureAgentRecommendedAccess runs.

andromedaapiAgentOnboardingReadiness.description:
AgentOnboardingReadiness is the computed onboarding classification for one
agent. It is recomputed on each assess call (not persisted in this phase).

runAll.title:
If true, run all enabled models regardless of the models list
By default, run_all gets triggered with all tenants and recompute true

success.title: true if the action was successfully applied

andromedaapiMatchSourceMessageMatchSourc.description:
- MATCH_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED: Not set.
 - HEURISTIC: Matched by the equivalence heuristic (name/slug/host scoring).
 - SELF: The discovered app is itself already onboarded (maps to itself).
 - OVERRIDE: Matched because a user set an explicit override for this discovered app.

jmlPolicyRuntimeId.description: Same JmlPolicyRuntime id; new action rows are created under this runtime.

attemptCount.description: Zero-indexed attempt number for the newly created action runtimes (1 for the first rerun).

timestamp.description:
timestamp is the UTC time the gateway observed the tool call, e.g.
2026-05-26T07:25:23.787021Z.

tenantId.description: tenant_id is the tenant that owns the gateway event, e.g. "chipotle".

requestId.description:
request_id is the gateway request identifier, e.g.
"7c922845-fe1e-4ee9-b909-c3d3ce392a6f".

delegatorSubject.description: delegator_subject is the human OBO token subject, e.g. "alice@example.com".

sessionId.description:
session_id groups tool calls that belong to the same agent conversation or
Cooper session, e.g. "sess-01JZ...".

agentId.description: agent_id is the identifier for the calling agent, e.g. "blackbox-agent".

agentName.description: agent_name is the display name for the calling agent, e.g. "Contract Review Copilot".

applicationId.description: application_id is the control-plane ToolApplication id, e.g. "app_123".

applicationSlug.description:
application_slug is the datapath route slug formerly stored as mcp_server,
e.g. "github-prod".

applicationName.description:
application_name is the display name of the governed application, e.g.
"GitHub Enterprise".

toolName.description: tool_name is the MCP tool invoked on the application, e.g. "repos_list".

policyId.description:
policy_id is the access policy that authorized or denied the call, e.g.
"policy_abc".

callIndex.description: call_index is the position of this tool call within the session, e.g. 3.

httpStatus.description: http_status is the upstream HTTP status observed by the gateway, e.g. 200.

status.description:
status is the policy DECISION for the call, e.g. ALLOW. It says nothing
about how the call then went - that is outcome. Unchanged in meaning and in
numbering since the axes were split, so stored values need no rewrite.

credentialMode.description: credential_mode is the outbound credential mode, e.g. "oauth_obo".

sourceIp.description: source_ip is the client IP observed by the gateway, e.g. "10.1.44.2".

latencyMs.description:
latency_ms is the end-to-end request latency in milliseconds as measured by
Envoy (time to last downstream tx byte), e.g. 142. Nullable: NULL for rows
written before Envoy access logging landed.

modelIntent.description:
model_intent is the agent-declared, free-text purpose for the call, captured
from the injected _andromeda_model_intent argument, e.g. File the bug report
the user asked for in repo acme-widgets. SIGNAL ONLY: recorded for audit and
risk review, never an input to the authorization decision. Empty when the
agent omitted it or the tool predates intent capture. Not low-cardinality:
this is high-cardinality free text.

userIntent.description:
user_intent is the original end-user request that started the session, echoed
by the agent, e.g. Summarize the attached quarterly report PDF. Constant
across a session; recover the session origin with
argMin(user_intent, timestamp) GROUP BY session_id. SIGNAL ONLY: recorded for
audit and risk review, never an input to the authorization decision. Empty
when not captured. Not low-cardinality: high-cardinality free text.

outcome.description:
outcome is what happened to the call once policy had decided, e.g. SUCCESS
for an allowed call the upstream answered 2xx, or ERROR for a JIT step-up
whose raise to the control plane failed. Orthogonal to status. Rows written
before the axes were split carry UNSPECIFIED permanently: there is no
backfill, and the read path reports them as having no outcome rather than
inferring one, so only events a gateway recorded an outcome for carry one.

errorReason.description:
error_reason explains a failed call in one line, e.g. jsonrpc -32603:
Internal error, or UF (upstream connection failure): connect timeout. Its
source depends on where the call broke: the upstream's own JSON-RPC or tool
error for an MCP failure, the control-plane message for a step-up that could
not be raised, and Envoy's response flags for a transport failure. Empty
whenever outcome is not ERROR. Not low-cardinality: upstream error text is
effectively free text.

andromedaclickhouseGatewayEvent.description:
GatewayEvent is the ClickHouse storage row for gateway tool-call audit events,
e.g. one Cooper datapath tools/call invocation.

andromedaclickhouseGatewayEventStatusMes.description:
- ERROR: ERROR: no decision recorded (ext_authz did not run).
 - JIT: JIT: gated behind a step-up and routed to the JIT handler, so the
upstream application was never called on this request.

Explorer remediation only: accept ASSIGNED reviews with this AI recommendation.

provisioning config, invalid access request profile, or an unsupported provider type).

Provider ids to update. Providers may be of different types (Okta, AWS, Entra, etc.);
each is dispatched to its type-specific configuration handler.

Full s3://bucket/key URI to the release ZIP. The bucket is part of the

fallbackReviewerId.description: Copied to the generated CampaignTemplate when set (same semantics as on campaign templates).

explorerView.description:
Explorer view context at campaign creation time (filters, provider scope, category).
Persisted on the generated campaign template as explorer_view_configuration.

campaignName.description: Display name for the created campaign instance and template (derived from explorer_view.name).

fallbackReviewerId.description: Copied to the generated CampaignTemplate when set (same semantics as on campaign templates).

campaignMode.description:
NOTIFICATION_ONLY (or unset) keeps the plain due-for-rotation reminder. NOTIFICATION_AND_KEY_CREATION
additionally creates a replacement key via relay for each due key and marks the old one for
decommissioning, leaving it in place. ROTATE_AND_DECOMMISSION goes one step further: after the old
key has been quiet past its deletion cooldown, its reviewer is asked to decommission (hard-delete)
or keep it. Example: NOTIFICATION_AND_KEY_CREATION.

campaignType.description:
Campaign type of the generated template. Must be set explicitly to NHI_KEY_ROTATION_CAMPAIGN;
no other value is accepted and there is no default. The in rule below pins the enum number for
NHI_KEY_ROTATION_CAMPAIGN, which also rejects the proto3 default of UAR_CAMPAIGN.
Example: NHI_KEY_ROTATION_CAMPAIGN.

ownerIdentityIds.description:
Andromeda identity UUIDs set as the campaign owners on the generated template
(campaign_owner_templates identity_template). At least one owner is required on both create and
update; there is no implicit default and the calling identity is never used as a fallback.
Example: 3f1c8b2a-8f0e-4c2a-9c1e-2b7d5a6f0e11.

providerId.title: Optional - not required for global schedules (policy.is_global = true)

dynamicClientRegistered.description:
Whether Andromeda registered an OAuth client for itself on the upstream
authorization server via RFC 7591 while serving this create. Meaningful only
under client_registration_mode DYNAMIC and always false under MANUAL, where
Andromeda registers nothing. When true the connection now needs per-user OAuth
consent before it can be used, and an McpDynamicClientRegistration row exists.

Discovery details are NOT repeated here - the caller already has them from
DiscoverToolApplicationAuth, which is what it used to decide how to populate
this request. Example: true

dynamicClientRegistrationError.title:
Why RFC 7591 registration failed when it was requested. Scoped strictly to
registration: it never reports an ordinary create validation error, which comes
back as a gRPC status instead. Empty under MANUAL, where no registration is
attempted, and empty when dynamic_client_registered is true.
Example: authorization server rejected the registration request

taskDefinitions.title: Embedded task definitions with DAG (used by generic composer)

requiredFeatureFlags.title: Feature flags required for this workflow to be created

Workflow ID for the deletion workflow (can be monitored via GetWorkflow API)

Provider deletion from config DB still succeeded, but cleanup workflow was not created

outcome.description: Which branch the onboarding UI should render.

discoveredAuth.description:
What the chain found. Empty for NO_AUTH_REQUIRED and NOT_DISCOVERABLE. For
OPERATOR_CLIENT_REQUIRED it carries the authorize and token endpoints, so the
operator pastes a client id and secret rather than also hunting for URLs.

errorMessage.title:
Why discovery stopped short. Empty unless outcome is NOT_DISCOVERABLE.
Example: 401 carried no resource_metadata and no protected-resource document was served

- NO_AUTH_REQUIRED: Unauthenticated initialize succeeded - the upstream needs no credentials.
Example: outcome NO_AUTH_REQUIRED
 - SELF_REGISTRATION_AVAILABLE: OAuth-protected and the authorization server advertises a
registration_endpoint. Example: outcome SELF_REGISTRATION_AVAILABLE
 - OPERATOR_CLIENT_REQUIRED: OAuth-protected, but no registration_endpoint - a client has to be created
by hand on the upstream and supplied to us. The discovered token and
authorize endpoints are still returned so the operator pastes fewer fields.
Named for that operator-supplied client, not for the OAuth
client_credentials grant, which is unrelated.
Example: outcome OPERATOR_CLIENT_REQUIRED
 - NOT_DISCOVERABLE: No protected-resource metadata at any layout, so nothing could be
discovered. The caller falls back to fully manual configuration.
Example: outcome NOT_DISCOVERABLE

The provider to simulate against. Required, and must match the one used for
the SimulateNhiRules call these pages belong to — a different provider is a

Return only these kinds of change. Empty means only the impactful kinds
(HUMAN_TO_SERVICE, SERVICE_TO_HUMAN, NHI_SUBTYPE_CHANGED) — the default a

email.description:
Email can either be of a SSO User, or a non-SSO User. The type of
User (SSO/non-SSO) is determined by checking the domain in the Email.
A non-SSO User is logged in via an OTP to the Email.
An SSO User on the other hand is logged in by redirecting it to
the configured IdP.

returnUrl.description:
ReturnURL is an optional setting for the API Client, that sets
the URL to which the User should return to after a successful
SAML Login. This applies for when the Email is that of an SSO-User.

apiLoginRequest.description:
LoginRequest is the main input payload that is provided by the User
on the login page.

apiLoginScheme.description:
- LOGIN_SCHEME_EMAIL_OTP: OTP is the default login scheme for non-SSO Users.
 - LOGIN_SCHEME_SAML: SAML is the login scheme for SSO Users.

email.description:
Email is the email of the User who wishes to access Andromeda resources.
Email is optional in AccessKeyLogin, and required in EmailLogin and SAMLLogin.

code.description:
Code is determined by what authentication flow is being used.
If the Login is initiated via the OTP flow, the code is the OTP sent on mail.
If the Login is initiated via the SAML flow, the code is what the IdP provides
post the redirects.
IF the Login is via the Access key flow, the code is the generated access key.

apiLoginVerificationRequest.description:
LoginVerificationRequest is the request payload that is provided by
Users while logging in.

resource.title:
Canonical resource identifier from protected-resource metadata. Sent as the
RFC 8707 resource parameter on authorize and token requests so the issued
token is audience-bound to this upstream and not replayable elsewhere.
NOT necessarily equal to the MCP server URL - PayPal advertises the origin
for a server at /mcp while Linear advertises the full path - so validate it
against the server ORIGIN, never by string equality.
Example: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp

issuer.title:
Authorization server issuer named by the resource. Attacker-influenced
input: it is supplied by the upstream, not by us, so a hostile MCP server can
point us at an authorization server it controls. Surfaced to the operator for
that reason. Every DCR-capable server surveyed co-locates this with the MCP
server URL, so an origin mismatch is the anomalous shape and is flagged.
Example: https://mcp.linear.app

authorizationEndpoint.title:
RFC 8414 authorization_endpoint - where the user consent redirect goes.
Example: https://mcp.linear.app/authorize

tokenEndpoint.title:
RFC 8414 token_endpoint - where codes and refresh tokens are exchanged.
Example: https://mcp.linear.app/token

registrationEndpoint.title:
RFC 7591 registration_endpoint. Empty means the upstream supports discovery
but not dynamic client registration, so a client has to be created by hand on
the upstream and supplied to us.
Example: https://mcp.linear.app/register

scopesSupported.title:
Scopes the resource advertises, which is the scope set the subsequent
registration sends: there is no shared scope vocabulary across upstreams
(read/write vs org:read vs a single opaque value), and some servers advertise
none at all - in which case scope is omitted from the registration request
entirely rather than guessed. Example: [read, write]

apiMcpDiscoveredAuth.description:
McpDiscoveredAuth reports what the unauthenticated discovery chain learned
about an upstream MCP server's authorization server: a 401 carrying
WWW-Authenticate, then RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, then RFC 8414
authorization-server metadata. Design: specs/agents/COOPER_OUTBOUND_DCR.md.

Response payload only, never persisted. CreateToolApplicationConnection re-runs
the chain server-side rather than accepting one of these back from the caller,
since client-supplied metadata must not steer an outbound registration. So a
stored copy would only ever be a staler version of what the next step re-fetches,
and the values that outlive onboarding land on AppOAuth3LeggedAuth and
McpDynamicClientRegistration instead.

id.title:
Falcon host group id, the value written into CROWDSTRIKE_RTR_INCLUDE_GROUP_IDS.
Eg. 1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d

name.title:
Group name as shown in Falcon.
Eg. Production Servers

description.title:
Group description, empty when the customer did not set one.
Eg. All production Linux hosts

rule.description:
The rule, supplied inline by the UI's rule editor or by an operator
testing a hypothesis.

label.description:
Optional label for this candidate in the response. Defaults to the rule
name. Useful when simulating several unnamed inline variants at once.

rule.description: The rule as simulated, echoed back so the caller can see exactly what ran.

sampleChanges.description:
A sample of affected users, capped by sample_limit. Impactful changes are
listed first so the sample is not filled with no-ops. Use
ListNhiRuleSimulationChanges to page the rest.

sampleTruncated.description:
True when the sample was cut short by sample_limit, so the UI never
implies the list is complete.

error.description:
Set when the candidate could not be simulated at all — an uncompilable
CEL expression, or a rule with no action. The candidate is reported with
this populated instead of failing the whole request, so one bad rule in a
batch does not hide the others' results.

rulesBefore.description:
Ids of the rules credited with the classification before and after. A
reviewer uses this to see which existing rule the candidate is competing
with.

apiNhiSimulationChange.description:
One user affected by a candidate rule, with enough identifying detail for a
reviewer to judge whether the change is right.

usersEvaluated.description: Users considered. Includes users excluded from the other counts by drift.

usersSkipped.description:
Users the engine could not evaluate at all, and which are therefore in no
other count here — not even users_evaluated. Normally 0.

When it is not 0 every other number below describes a smaller population
than the provider actually has, so it is reported rather than only logged:
a caller comparing changed_total against its own idea of the provider size
would otherwise silently under-read the blast radius.

candidateMatched.description:
Users whose attributes satisfied the candidate's predicate, whether or
not anything changed for them.

changedTotal.description:
Users whose classification actually differs. The sum of
human_to_service, service_to_human and nhi_subtype_changed.

baselineDrift.description:
Users whose current stored classification could not be reproduced by
replaying the tenant's existing rules. Something outside the rule engine
set their label, so the simulated outcome for them cannot be trusted; they
are excluded from every other count above except users_evaluated.

A large number here is a warning about the simulation, not about the
candidate rule. Surface it to the reviewer rather than hiding it.

confirmsExistingNhi.description:
Agreement between the candidate and the classification the tenant already
has, over the users the candidate matched. A rule that only ever confirms
existing NHIs changes nothing if saved; one producing a large new_nhi count
is either exactly what was intended or an over-broad rule, and the sampled
user list is how a reviewer tells those apart.

apiNhiSimulationCounts.description:
Exact impact counts for one candidate over the whole user population. Every
number here is a full count, never an estimate or a sample.

apiOnDemandAnalysisType.description:
OnDemandAnalysisType identifies which analysis to run via TriggerOnDemandAnalysis.
Add a new value here when a new on-demand analysis is wired up.

 - IDP_GROUP_OUTLIER: Group IDP anomaly detection — runs ariel's GroupMemberAnomalyWorkflow for the given tenant.
 - DORMANT_GROUPS: Dormant groups detection — runs ariel's GroupDormantWorkflow for the given tenant.
 - RISK_RECOMPUTE: Full tenant risk recomputation — runs kuiper's risk trigger (the same
ExecutionService method knot fires after each inventory sync), recomputing
the entire tenant risk pipeline. Heavy; prefer AGENT_RISK_RECOMPUTE for
agent-link-driven refreshes.
 - AGENT_RISK_RECOMPUTE: Scoped agent risk recomputation — runs only the agent-affecting steps
(agent risk + effective risk) rather than the whole tenant pipeline. Fired
when an inventory provider link changes so agent effective risk reflects
the new operator bound without a full tenant recompute.

tenantId.title:
Tenant that owns the agents.
Example: 9c719c8f-bf6c-40cd-80bd-e18f671411f3

agentIds.title:

of one). Example: [a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890]

Per-agent acceptance outcome, one entry per requested agent id. With the
async backend these describe acceptance/synchronous rejection (ACCEPTED /
SKIPPED_NOT_ELIGIBLE / already-in-progress), not the final onboarding result;
the async outcome is read from the agent onboarding_workflow_id + state.

errorDetails.description: Set only when the request could not be processed at all (e.g. bad input).

workflowId.title:
Knot workflow id of the run created for the accepted agents; empty when no
agent was accepted (all skipped). Lets a caller query the run-level rollup
(GetWorkflowMetrics) without re-reading agent nodes.
Example: wf-01HY5F4K2K8M8N8Z4Y3Q6QJ7M9

applicationId.title:
ToolApplication id this entry covers.
Example: 1f2e3d4c-5b6a-7890-1234-567890abcdef

applicationName.title:
Display name of the application carried from the catalog.
Example: GitHub

resourceConditions.title:
Optional resource conditions scoped to this application (same shape the
policy create path persists). Only valid when inventory_linked is true.
Example: attribute resource_path operator NOT_IN values [acme/prod-api]

rationale.title:
One-line rationale for why this application and these tools were chosen.
Example: Read-only access to sales repos for report generation

inventoryLinked.title:
Whether the application is linked to an inventory provider. Resource
conditions are only meaningful (and only enforced) when this is true.
Example: true

apiPolicyAuthorApplicationEntry.description:
PolicyAuthorApplicationEntry is the proposed access to a single application:
the tools to allow plus optional resource conditions (e.g. exclude prod repos).

suggestedBundleName.title:
Suggested bundle name.

suggestedDescription.title:
Suggested bundle description.
Example: Read-only sales data access for quarterly reporting

warnings.title:
Non-fatal warnings for the admin to review (e.g. high-risk tools included,
catalog truncated, resource conditions skipped for unlinked apps).
Example: delete_repository is high-risk and was excluded

apiPolicyAuthorProposal.description: PolicyAuthorProposal is the editable bundle the agent proposes.

intent.title:
Natural-language description of what the agent should be able to do.
Example: a sales agent that curates the quarterly sales report

priorProposal.description:
Optional: the proposal returned by a previous turn, echoed back so the agent
can refine it instead of starting over.

refineInstruction.title:
Optional: a follow-up instruction to revise the prior proposal.
