keyId.description:
Non-sensitive companion identifier for the created credential (e.g. AWS's IAM access key
id). The sensitive secret value itself never leaves the broker.

secretFingerprint.description:
One-way fingerprint of the sensitive credential value only (e.g. the IAM secret access
key alone, not the {access_key_id, secret_access_key} pair). Format: "sha256:" +
hex(sha256(value)). Lets a caller verify/compare against a specific issued secret later
without ever being able to reconstruct it.

warnings.description:
Advisory, non-fatal information (e.g. the identity is now at the provider's max
credential count). Empty when there's nothing to flag. Never used for failures.

keyName.description:
The display name actually set on the provider-side credential, when that key type has a
display-name concept (e.g. an Entra password credential, a GCP API key) - either the
caller-supplied key_name echoed back, or the broker's own generated default when the caller
didn't supply one. Empty for key types with no display-name concept (e.g. AWS IAM access
keys, GCP service account keys). Distinct from secret_name, which is the vault secret's own
name/path, not a provider-side display name.

executionRef.description:
Execution reference returned by the remote service after a successful StartExecution call.
Encoded as JSON containing both the endpoint and the remote execution_id so that
TaskState and Stop calls remain resilient across knot restarts.

sync.description:
When true, knot uses the synchronous Execute RPC: the remote service runs
the method and returns, and knot manages state locally via goroutines/channels.
When false (default), knot uses the legacy async pattern:
StartExecution → poll GetExecutionStatus → CancelExecution.

orchestratorGrpcInvocation.description:

the ExecutionService gRPC contract (andromeda.nonpublic.orchestrator.ExecutionService).

inline.title: Build Job entirely from these fields

args.title: Per-execution arguments, rendered as --key=value and replacing the container's args

timeoutMinutes.description:
Optional: override activeDeadlineSeconds on the created Job (minutes).
If 0, inherits from template (TEMPLATE mode) or no deadline (INLINE mode).

jobName.title: Populated after the Job is created — used for tracking across knot restarts

orchestratorKubernetesInvocation.description:
TEMPLATE mode (from_cronjob): Derives the Job from an existing CronJob deployed via
  Helm. Knot reads the CronJob's .spec.jobTemplate and overrides the container args.
  All operational config (resources, affinity, labels, secrets) stays in Helm.
  Use for established executors that already have a Helm chart (e.g., lsp-eps, risk).

  INLINE mode (inline): Self-contained Job spec defined entirely in this message.
  Knot builds the Job from scratch. Use for new services that don't have a Helm chart,
  or for ad-hoc one-off jobs.
orchestratorKubernetesInvocation.title:
KubernetesInvocation defines the configuration for running a task as a Kubernetes Job.
Supports two modes via the job_source oneof:

cronjobName.description: Name of the CronJob (e.g., "lsp-eps"). Must exist in the target namespace.

orchestratorKubernetesJobFromCronJob.description:
KubernetesJobFromCronJob sources the Job spec from an existing CronJob.
The CronJob should be deployed via Helm with suspend: true so it acts
purely as a template — knot controls when Jobs are created.

ttlSecondsAfterFinished.title: TTL for automatic cleanup after Job finishes (default: 120 seconds)

labels.title: Labels applied to the Job and pod template (key-value pairs)

env.title: Environment variables injected into the container (key-value pairs)

orchestratorKubernetesJobInline.description:
KubernetesJobInline defines a self-contained Job spec for services without a Helm chart.
Knot constructs the full Kubernetes Job from these fields.

workflowDefinitionId.title: Foreign key to the workflow definition (template) that will be instantiated

tenantId.title:
Tenant ID - the tenant context for workflow instances created from this schedule
Optional for global schedules (when policy.is_global = true)
Required for tenant-specific schedules

providerId.title:
Provider ID - the provider context for workflow instances created from this schedule
Optional for global schedules (when policy.is_global = true) and tenant-wide workflows
Required for provider-specific schedules

policy.title:
Schedule policy defining execution mode and overlap handling
Required field that determines scheduling behavior

cronExpression.title:
Cron expression for TIME_BASED mode (e.g., "0 */6 * * *" for every 6 hours)
Required when policy.mode = TIME_BASED
Ignored when policy.mode = AUTO_CAPACITY
Uses standard cron format: minute hour day month weekday

enabled.title:
Whether the schedule is currently active
False = paused (won't trigger), True = active
Allows pausing schedules without deletion

nextExecutionAt.title:
Pre-calculated next execution time for efficient polling
Updated after each execution or when schedule is modified
Indexed for fast "get schedules ready to run" queries

maxExecutions.title:
Maximum number of times this schedule should execute
0 or NULL = unlimited executions (default for recurring schedules)
> 0 = schedule will stop after this many executions
Example: Set to 7 for a daily backup that runs for one week
Works with execution_count to track progress

executionCount.title:
Counter tracking how many times this schedule has been triggered
Used for monitoring, debugging, and enforcing max_executions
Reset to 0 when schedule is created or manually reset

orchestratorSchedule.title:
Schedule defines a scheduled workflow execution
Supports both auto-capacity scheduling and time-based (cron) scheduling

mode.title: Scheduling mode: AUTO_CAPACITY (knot decides when based on capacity) or TIME_BASED (runs at specific time)

overlapPolicy.title: Policy for handling overlapping executions when schedule triggers while previous run is still executing

timezone.title:
Timezone for cron evaluation (IANA timezone name, e.g., "America/New_York", "UTC", "Asia/Kolkata")
Defaults to "UTC" if not specified or empty
Only applies to FIXED_TIME mode
The cron expression will be evaluated in this timezone to determine next execution time

runImmediately.title:
If true, triggers an immediate execution when schedule is first created/enabled
After the immediate execution, follows normal cron schedule
Useful for "populate now, then keep updated" scenarios
Only applies to FIXED_TIME mode

isGlobal.title:
If true, this is a global schedule that operates across all tenants
Global schedules do not require tenant_id or provider_id
Used for system-wide operations like query cache, cleanup jobs, etc.
When true, tenant_id and provider_id in Schedule message are ignored/optional

frequency.title:
Schedule frequency: DAILY_ONCE, HOURLY, EVERY_6_HOURS, etc.
This is a higher-level abstraction that can be translated to cron expressions
If UNSPECIFIED, the schedule will use the existing mechanism

forceFullSync.title:
If true, workflows triggered by this schedule will perform a full sync
instead of incremental sync. This resets all resources to INITIATED state
and re-fetches all data from the provider.
Default: false (incremental sync)

orchestratorSchedulePolicy.title: SchedulePolicy defines how the schedule should be executed and handled

executionId.description:
Stable identifier assigned by the remote service for this execution.
Knot stores this and passes it back in subsequent GetExecutionStatus and
CancelExecution calls.

providerId.title: Provider ID for the task (optional)

name.title: Task name (must be unique within the workflow)

needs.title: Task dependencies - list of task names that must complete before this task

retryWaitSeconds.title:
Retry configuration - constant wait time between retries (in seconds)
Default: 0 (no retry wait, immediate requeue)

maxRetries.title:
Maximum number of retry attempts before marking as FAILED
Default: 0 (no retries allowed)

allowPartialDependencyFailure.title:
Allow partial dependency failure - if true, task can run if at least one dependency succeeds
If false (default), ALL dependencies must succeed for task to run
Use case: Tenant logical layer should run even if some provider workflows fail

consumeDependencyResults.description:
When true, knot collects results from dependency tasks
and injects them into this task's invocation args as DependencyResult_<task_name> keys.

timeRangeAware.description:
When true, knot looks up the most recent COMPLETED run of this (type, tenant, provider)
and injects its start_time as LastSuccessfulStartTime + CurrentRunStartTime.
Only set this for tasks that do incremental/time-range queries (delta sync, etc.).

fanOut.description:
Fan-out configuration: controls how this template task expands into N concrete tasks.
When unset (nil), the task is a single concrete task with no expansion.

disabled.description:
When true, the generic composer skips this task during expansion.
Downstream tasks that depended on it lose that dependency but still run.

orchestratorTaskDefinition.title:
TaskDefinition defines a task within a workflow
This is used by both the API service (CreateWorkflowRequest) and internal models (AndromedaWorkflowInvocation)

orchestratorTaskInvocationDetails.title:
TaskInvocationDetails wraps the oneOf for runtime-specific invocation configuration
This creates a single JSONB column in SQL instead of one column per runtime type

workflowName.title: The name of the Temporal workflow function to execute (e.g., "InventoryFetchWorkflow")

workflowId.title: The actual Temporal workflow execution ID returned after starting the workflow

workflowArgs.title:
Workflow arguments as key-value pairs to be passed to the Temporal workflow
These will be merged with the task metadata when invoking the workflow

timeoutMinutes.title:
Timeout for the Temporal workflow execution in minutes
This sets the WorkflowExecutionTimeout when invoking the workflow
Default: 720 (12 hours) if not specified or 0

id.title: Unique identifier for this workflow definition

name.title:
Human-readable name for this workflow definition
This will be used as a base name for workflow instances

description.title: Description of what this workflow does

priority.title: Default priority for workflow instances created from this definition

taskDefinitions.description:
Embedded task definitions with dependency graph (DAG).
When present, the generic composer expands these into concrete tasks at schedule trigger time.
When absent, the legacy ComposerRegistry path is used.
Stored as JSONB.

requiredFeatureFlags.description:
Feature flags that must all be ENABLED for the tenant before the workflow is created.
Checked by the poller before invoking the composer.
If any flag is not enabled, the workflow is skipped entirely.

orchestratorWorkflowDefinition.title:
WorkflowDefinition represents a reusable workflow template
This is the "blueprint" for workflows that can be instantiated multiple times
Used by: Scheduler, Manual triggers, API calls

workflowDefinitionId.title: Reference to the workflow definition this task belongs to

name.title: Task name (must be unique within the workflow definition)

runtime.title: Runtime for this task (e.g., TEMPORAL, ORCHESTRATOR_LOCAL)

invocationDetails.title:
Runtime-specific invocation configuration
Stored as a single JSONB column containing the runtime type and its configuration

orchestratorWorkflowTaskDefinition.title:
WorkflowTaskDefinition represents a task definition within a workflow definition
This is the reusable task blueprint that gets instantiated as Task when workflow runs

allResourceAccessLevels.title: Policies with allResources=true for a service type — apply to every resource

policyId.title: ID of the policy, empty if policies were processed as a group

resourcesData.title: Resource data grouped by service type (e.g. S3, EC2)

policyPolicyResourcesData.title: PolicyResourcesData contains resource data for a single policy or policy group

policiesResourcesData.title: Resource data for each policy/policy group that was analyzed

policyResourcesDataResponse.title: ResourcesDataResponse contains resource data for each policy or policy group

serviceType.title:
Service type scope for all_resource_access_levels entries. If non-empty, this entry applies
only to resources whose service type matches this value (e.g. "ec2"). Empty means all resources.
Example: "ec2"

policyTagConstraint.description:
TagConstraint describes a single tag the policy is gated on.
Example: tag_type AWS_REQUEST, key environment, values [preprod, production].

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

protobufNullValue.description:
`NullValue` is a singleton enumeration to represent the null value for the
`Value` type union.

The JSON representation for `NullValue` is JSON `null`.

 - NULL_VALUE: Null value.

providers that don't need it.

Example: https://org12345.crm.dynamics.com.

relayDetachAgentDirectConnectionsData.description: DetachAgentDirectConnectionsData carries the resolved inputs for the detach.

strategy.description:
Resolved from the eligibility's provision_via_nhi flag + provider type. v1: DEDICATED_NHI.
DEDICATED_NHI already implies issuing a single access key, so no credential strategy is
carried. The NHI gets no org role; the folders and per-folder role come from the request
resource_set_configuration / role_metadata, not from this message.

name.title: Resolved NHI name. Example: andromeda-jit-<accessRequestId>

ownerIdentityIds.title:
Owner(s) of the NHI in the Andromeda graph. In v1 always exactly one entry: the requester identity ID.
Example: ["d2f5d10b-0555-4721-bfc2-32aacb0a03ba"]

relayManagedNhiProvisioning.description:
ManagedNhiProvisioning is the per-request resolved instruction to provision a managed NHI
instead of a direct resource-set assignment. Presence of this field switches the resource-set
plugin into NHI mode; absence keeps the existing behavior byte-for-byte.

disabledPlanIds.description: servicePlanId GUIDs for Microsoft Graph assignLicense disabledPlans.

agentId.description:
Agent that was the binding principal for the provisioned access,
sourced from the access request agent_stepup_data.agent_id.

externalBindingId.description:
Polaris binding id returned as external_assignment_id on the
corresponding AddAgentAppAssignmentResponse. The plugin revokes by this
id; agent_id/role_metadata are carried for logging only.

idpProviderId.description: Idp Provider Id of the idp connected with the access request/review binding Provider.

managedNhiProvisioning.description: Optional. Presence switches deprovision into managed-NHI mode (delete the service account).

externalNhiId.title:
Provider-side id of the service account to delete (the deprovision handle). Required in NHI mode.
Deleting the SA cascades token deletion. Example: 42

provisioningCredentials.description: Reference to the secret store entry to scrub on deprovision (e.g. an ASM ARN).

agentId.description:
NHI principal for agent role bindings. Mutually exclusive with
user_id/group_id.

provisioningRoleName.title: pset name for the role assignment

externalBindingId.title: External ID of the role assignment binding (e.g., Azure transaction ID)

relayTicket.title: Ticket represents a ticket in the ITSM system

adUserData.description: Active Directory LDAP attribute values (keys are LDAP attribute names, e.g. givenName, mail).

entraUserData.description: Microsoft Entra ID user fields (keys match Microsoft Graph user property names, e.g. jobTitle, department).

oktaUserData.description: Okta user profile fields (JSON object keys match Okta profile attribute names).

secuarTriggerRevocationResponse.title: Response indicating success or failure of the revocation operation

name.description: English country name (e.g. "United States"). Same value returned by GetApproximateGeolocation.country_name.

SessionSummary is the status of each session summary triggered
by the ada session summarization service.

so the caller can deserialize based on the explorer view's category.

queryId.description: The unique ID of the registered query (mirrors descriptor.id).

dynamic.description: Dynamic cached query response — the payload is the category-specific connection proto.

activity.description:
Activity is the stringified JSON of the activity. This could be eiher the IdP activity,
or an action within the Provider or Account.

location.description:
Location is the geo location figured out from the Action. This typically comes as part
of the log itself, either in the form of source IPAddress, or the location details (for
instance in case of Okta logs).
In case the Provider/Integration logs do not provide this data, we query maxmind and store
the location internally while ingesting.

device.description: Device carries the device information that was used to carry out the Activity.

errorCode.title:
error_code is the resolved error code string from the error_lookup table
for the underlying log line. Example: AADSTS50126

errorString.title:
error_string is the human readable error message resolved from the
error_lookup table. Example: invalid username or password

isError.description:
is_error indicates whether the underlying log line is an error as resolved
from the error_lookup table. Some 2xx events are still classified as errors.

typeDayOfWeek.description:
Represents a day of the week.

 - DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED: The day of the week is unspecified.
 - MONDAY: Monday
 - TUESDAY: Tuesday
 - WEDNESDAY: Wednesday
 - THURSDAY: Thursday
 - FRIDAY: Friday
 - SATURDAY: Saturday
 - SUNDAY: Sunday

hours.description:
Hours of day in 24 hour format. Should be from 0 to 23. An API may choose
to allow the value "24:00:00" for scenarios like business closing time.

minutes.description: Minutes of hour of day. Must be from 0 to 59.

seconds.description:
Seconds of minutes of the time. Must normally be from 0 to 59. An API may
allow the value 60 if it allows leap-seconds.

nanos.description: Fractions of seconds in nanoseconds. Must be from 0 to 999,999,999.

typeTimeOfDay.description:
Represents a time of day. The date and time zone are either not significant
or are specified elsewhere. An API may choose to allow leap seconds. Related
types are [google.type.Date][google.type.Date] and
`google.protobuf.Timestamp`.

id.description: IANA Time Zone Database time zone, e.g. "America/New_York".

version.description: Optional. IANA Time Zone Database version number, e.g. "2019a".

typeTimeZone.description:
Represents a time zone from the
[IANA Time Zone Database](https://www.iana.org/time-zones).
